title: Fallback orchestration latency surge retrospective and hardening plan
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 we experienced a multi-region availability degradation triggered by an orchestrated fallback sequence that concentrated traffic into a single secondary region. The event produced sustained latency SLO misses (p95 generation latency crossed 600ms, target 200ms) and elevated error rates for 32 minutes for ~14% of hosted API traffic. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized hardening plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-27 09:17 UTC: Canary alarms triggered in region-eu; alert routed to on-call infra and serving teams.
2026-02-27 09:20 UTC: Automated failover policy started migrating traffic from region-eu to region-us-west due to region-eu transient scheduler stalls.

2026-02-27 09:23 UTC: Circuit breaker on region-us-west tripped open for a subset of model endpoints; traffic routed to fallback pool which was configured as single-region pool (region-us-east) by policy mis-evaluation.
2026-02-27 09:25–09:34 UTC: Region-us-east became overloaded; KV cache warmup latencies increased, cold-cache hits rose from 4% to 27% per request, compounding per-request latency.
2026-02-27 09:34 UTC: On-call team applied emergency traffic rebalancing throttle and widened circuit breaker thresholds to allow gradual ramp.
2026-02-27 09:49 UTC: Gradual recovery as caches warmed and autoscaling responded; SLOs returned under target by 10:05 UTC. Post-incident monitoring cleared by 10:20 UTC.
2026-02-27 11:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved; incident review started.
2026-02-28 15:00 UTC: Initial RCA draft completed and shared with reliability and product leadership.
detection: The degradation was detected by synthetic p95 latency canaries for the /v1/generate route in region-eu which breached the 200ms SLO. Alerting correctly escalated to on-call; however, runbook guidance routed to the standard failover flow which later amplified the issue.
root_cause: A combination of a policy evaluation bug in the fallback orchestration service and overly aggressive circuit-breaker default settings. When region-eu signaled degraded capacity, the orchestrator erroneously evaluated the fallback pool as a single-region candidate (region-us-east) due to cached policy TTL staleness, concentrating rerouted traffic. Circuit breakers tripped on region-us-west earlier than expected because thresholds did not account for short-lived bursty failovers. This led to cascading reroutes and cold-KV-cache amplification in the overloaded region.
contributing_factors: Fallback orchestration cached policy snapshot with TTL 10m — stale view excluded multi-region fallback pool nodes
Circuit breaker thresholds used fixed error-rate window that did not account for immediate transient retries during failover
Autoscaler cooldowns were conservative; vertical autoscaling for KV-cache nodes took longer than traffic ramp-up window
No explicit chaos / failover runbook tests for the current routing policy variants since last policy change two months ago
Monitoring lacked a cross-region aggregated inbound routing metric which would have shown traffic concentration earlier
mitigations_during_incident: Emergency manual override to re-enable multi-region fallback pools and immediate rollback of the stale policy cache
Increased circuit breaker retry budget and widened open-to-half-open transition thresholds for critical model endpoints
Applied temporary traffic shaping to cap new connections into region-us-east at 60% while allowing warm cache traffic to complete
Triggered manual warmup of KV caches by replaying recent prefixes against warmed instances
Scaled up KV-cache instances in region-us-east with accelerated provisioning script
action_items: A1: Reduce fallback orchestration policy cache TTL from 10m to 20s and add explicit policy freshness check before applying high-impact reroutes — owner: Priya Singh — due: 2026-03-10
A2: Add a routing pre-check that verifies fallback pool >= 2 regions before executing global failover; fail open to canary routing if check fails — owner: Kofi Mensah — due: 2026-03-17
A3: Rework circuit breaker thresholds to include a short-term burst-aware window and differentiate between client-origin retries and system-origin errors — owner: Elena Ruiz — due: 2026-03-24
A4: Implement cross-region traffic concentration alert (dashboard + PagerDuty) that fires when >50% of redirected traffic lands in a single region for >2 minutes — owner: SRE Team — due: 2026-03-12
A5: Create a failover chaos test matrix (policy variants x model families) and add to weekly e2e reliability tests — owner: Reliability Eng — due: 2026-04-07
A6: Shorten autoscaler cooldowns for KV-cache pool warmup path and add prioritized warmup slots for emergency failovers — owner: Infra Autoscale — due: 2026-03-31
A7: Update rollback playbook and runbook to include immediate policy cache invalidation and scrub of single-region fallback assignments — owner: Oncall Runbooks — due: 2026-03-09
A8: Produce evaluation report comparing routing decisions pre/post-policy TTL change to validate non-regression — owner: Observability — due: 2026-03-21
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: A1 work started; initial change to cache TTL is in a feature branch (github.com/redwood/reorg/pulls/1867).
2026-03-03: Observability added provisional dashboard panel for cross-region concentration (dashboard id: RL-447).
2026-03-05: SRE team ran simulated failover test; detected additional edge-case where fallback pool membership API returned 500 intermittently — ticket ENG-15487 opened.
2026-03-08: Priya deployed cache TTL 20s to staging and observed no regressions in policy consistency during staged failovers.
2026-03-10: Draft of circuit breaker threshold proposal completed and circulated for architecture review (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/KB/fallback-cb-design).
